subject: PoppyHealth dedicated capacity: throughput fit & ramp recommendation
messages:
From: Eve Turner <eve@poppyhealth.co>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity questions for pilot

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo this week — team loved the latency consistency. To move toward procurement we need a concrete capacity proposal we can budget against. Here are the rough usage profiles we expect for the MVP (US users):

- Peak concurrency: ~60 concurrent active sessions
- Peak requests/s: ~60 RPS (spikey: short bursts up to ~90 RPS)
- Average tokens per request (prompt + completion): ~750 tokens
- Target p95 end-to-end latency (API -> response stream ready): <= 350 ms for the happy path
- Traffic pattern: daily peaks 11:00-14:00 PT, shorter evening peaks; predictable weekday pattern

Based on the above our simple tokens/sec at peak is: 60 RPS * 750 tokens = 45,000 tokens/sec. We need a recommended Dedicated baseline (GUIs/Slabs) and a staged ramp plan for the first 30 days so procurement can size the commit. Also include assumptions (model variant, quantization, KV/prefix cache expectations).

I attached our internal TPS profiling (poppy_tps_profile.csv). Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Eve
Eve Turner
Head of Product
PoppyHealth

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Eve Turner <eve@poppyhealth.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions for pilot

Eve — thanks, that's super helpful. Looping in Ben (capacity modeling) and Irene (SRE/ops) to validate numbers. High-level comment before they chime in:

- Baseline compute ask (tokens/sec): 45k t/s (as you calculated).
- Assumptions we used for initial sizing:
  * Model: redwood/open-chat-large (quantized 4-bit inference path).
  * Measured sustained throughput per A100-style GPU at p95 for that model with our optimizations: ~3.0k tokens/sec. This includes prefix/KV caching at ~30% hit rate and continuous batching at typical request inter-arrivals.
  * Effective tokens/sec per GPU (post-cache): ~3.9k t/s (45k * (1 - 0.30) / GPUs -> see calc below).

Quick calc: with 30% cache hit, net tokens to execute = 45k * 0.7 = 31.5k t/s. At 3.0k sustained per GPU we need ~10.5 GPUs. We typically recommend 25-50% headroom for burstiness and parity with p95 SLOs -> round to 14 GPUs.

Recommendation (pilot -> committed):
- Pilot (week 0-2): Dedicated burst pool of 4 GPUs (on-demand) + hosted fallback. This lets you validate tail and cache behavior without commitment.
- Committed baseline (month 1 onward): 16 GPUs in a Dedicated pool, arranged as 2 x 8-GPU slabs. Why 16 vs 14? We prefer integer slab counts, plus an extra cushion for 30-40% unexpected spikes and to keep p95 latency under 350ms during business hours.
- Autoscaling/burst policy: enable auto-burst to shared capacity for short spikes (up to +50% for <10min) and an alert at 70% sustained utilization.

Latency expectations (p95):
- At sustained 60 RPS with 30% cache: expected p95 end-to-end ~300-340 ms (within target).
- At 90 RPS short bursts without cache warming: p95 can slip to ~480 ms — mitigated by cache pre-warm and the burst policy above.

I'll let Ben and Irene add any adjustments and attach a short runbook for pre-warming strategy. We'll follow up with a line-itemized cost estimate for 16 GPUs and contract language for burst allowances.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean — that level of detail is exactly what procurement needs. Two quick follow-ups from our side:

1) Can you provide the per-GPU throughput assumption (3.0k t/s) as an empirical reference (log / benchmark you ran) and clarify if that number assumes 4-bit quantization and KV-cache enabled?
2) What's the expected improvement if we switch to a smaller generation target (shorter completions) — e.g., avg tokens drops from 750 to 450?

If the pilot burst plan looks good we'll sign the pilot order and then move to a 12-18 month committed slab for the baseline.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Eve
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Eve Turner <eve@poppyhealth.co>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions for pilot

Sean / Eve — quick note with the benchmark pointers and a compact action plan.

Benchmarks:
- Empirical per-GPU figures (redwood/open-chat-large, 4-bit quantized, batching=dynamic): sustained p95 throughput = 3.0k t/s, p50 bursts up to ~4.8k t/s for short windows (10-30s) before KV-cache effects dominate. These numbers come from our internal perf bench harness (run id: perf-20270518-ochl). I'll share the perf snapshot in the deal folder.

Sensitivity (if avg tokens -> 450):
- New token demand at 60 RPS = 60 * 450 = 27k t/s. With 30% cache that becomes 18.9k t/s. At 3.0k t/s steady per GPU -> ~6.3 GPUs -> recommend 8 GPUs committed (one 8-GPU slab) + 1-2 GPU burst cushion. So shorter completions materially reduce committed footprint.

Staged ramp proposal (concrete):
- Day 0-7 (pilot): 4 GPUs burst-capable (hosted + Dedicated burst) — validate cache hit ~30% and measure tail.
- Day 8-21 (scale): increase to 8 GPUs Dedicated (1 slab) if measured net t/s <= 20k; if still near 30k require move to 16 GPUs.
- Day 22+: move to committed 16 GPUs (2 slabs) only if observed sustained post-cache >= ~28k t/s and p95 > 350ms with 8 GPUs.

Ops notes: pre-warm plan = batch a rolling sequence of top-100 prefixes over 30 minutes before business hours; target KV hit to 35-40% prior to peak. Also enable short-lived burst pool (+50% capacity) for first 4 weeks to absorb calibration errors.

Action items:
- Sean: include this ramp schedule in the procurement SOW and cost sheet (Irene, can you attach the runbook?).
- Irene: please add runbook link and cost delta for 8->16 GPU transition.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Modeling, Redwood Inference
